runs.market_commentary:
Asian markets opened the week on the back foot, with the Nikkei 225 declining 0.7% to close at 65,528 as technology stocks pulled back ahead of Nvidia's highly anticipated earnings report later this week. The pressure on semis and AI-adjacent names in Tokyo reflected caution ahead of both Nvidia results and the Federal Reserve's Jackson Hole Symposium, two event risks that have kept institutional traders sidelined. Broader Asia was mixed; the Hang Seng held modestly while South Korean and Taiwanese tech names tracked the Nikkei lower.

European markets opened with a cautious tone, the DAX shedding roughly 0.3% and the FTSE 100 off 0.2% as investors digested weekend news that US-Canada trade negotiations have broken down again, raising fresh tariff escalation fears. ECB chief economist Philip Lane's August 18 comments - warning that euro-area inflation will hover near 3% for the rest of 2026 - continued to weigh on rate-sensitive European sectors, with the deposit rate held at 2.25% in July and a September move increasingly priced in by bond markets.

US pre-market futures are modestly negative ahead of Monday's open: S&P 500 futures off 0.1%, Nasdaq 100 futures down 0.4%, and Dow futures sliding 0.1% as the Trump administration finalizes details of new economic sanctions against Iran, adding an oil-supply risk premium that is supporting WTI crude around $83.45. The 10-year Treasury yield sits at 4.28% with the Fed funds target at 3.50-3.75% following July's 9-3 vote favoring a hold, but with three dissenters pushing for an immediate 25bp hike - a divide that makes this week's Jackson Hole speeches the most market-moving Fed event of the summer. Domestically, Case-Shiller home price data and new home sales are the morning's key data releases, read primarily as inflation signals given shelter's outsized weight in CPI.

ideas.catalyst: Nvidia reports quarterly earnings this week with Wall Street expecting record data-center revenue driven by Blackwell GPU demand.
ideas.thesis: NVDA has been the central pillar of the AI infrastructure buildout, and any earnings beat with raised guidance would drive a sharp short-squeeze given the positioning overhang from the pre-Jackson-Hole pullback. The Nasdaq's -0.4% pre-market slip creates an attractive risk/reward entry point before the print.
ideas.key_risk: A revenue miss or cautious margin guidance around Blackwell yields could send NVDA -10% or more given its elevated multiple.

ideas.catalyst: Goldman Sachs added AON to its August Conviction Buy list with a $430 price target implying 21% upside, citing NFP acquisition synergies and above-consensus 2026 FCF.
ideas.thesis: Goldman's conviction list addition provides a near-term institutional demand catalyst, while AON's operational leverage from the NFP integration and strong organic growth pipeline make the risk/reward asymmetric to the upside. ideas.theme: Biotech Downside / FDA Rejection + Activist Pressure
ideas.catalyst: FDA advisory panel voted 9-3 against deramiocel for DMD-related cardiomyopathy; activist Kaos Capital is demanding board overhaul and capital restructuring.
ideas.thesis: With its lead asset rejected by an FDA advisory committee and now facing a board overhaul campaign from Kaos Capital, Capricor is in capital-preservation mode with a de-risked pipeline and uncertain future. The stock is likely to remain under heavy selling pressure as institutional holders reassess the binary-event loss.
ideas.key_risk: A surprise FDA approval despite the advisory panel vote or a white-knight acquisition approach could create a sharp short-covering squeeze.

ideas.thesis: Capital One sits at the intersection of consumer credit recovery and rate normalization, two themes Goldman expects to accelerate into year-end. Its Discover integration synergies provide an additional earnings lever not yet fully reflected in consensus estimates.
ideas.key_risk: A consumer credit deterioration or surprise Fed rate hike could spike COF's net charge-offs and pressure the stock regardless of Goldman's conviction.

ideas.theme: Geopolitical Risk / Iran Sanctions Oil Spike
ideas.catalyst: The Trump administration is finalizing new economic sanctions against Iran, adding an oil-supply risk premium supporting WTI at $83.45.
ideas.thesis: Iran sanctions restricting oil exports would tighten the global supply-demand balance at a time when OPEC+ has limited spare capacity, providing a structural bid for energy equities. XLE offers diversified exposure to US majors and E&Ps with leverage to crude prices.
ideas.key_risk: A diplomatic de-escalation or unexpected OPEC+ production increase could quickly unwind any geopolitically-driven oil premium.

ideas.theme: Fed Policy Risk / Jackson Hole Hawkish Surprise
ideas.catalyst: July Fed minutes showed a 9-3 vote with three dissenters pushing for an immediate 25bp hike; Jackson Hole speeches this week could cement hawkish expectations.
ideas.thesis: With the Fed split showing meaningful dissent and ECB also warning of persistent inflation near 3%, the bond market faces a hawkish surprise risk at Jackson Hole not fully priced into the current 4.28% 10-year yield. A TLT short hedges both Jackson Hole risk and any stronger-than-expected inflation data.
ideas.key_risk: A dovish pivot or recessionary data surprises could spark a rapid bond rally, creating significant mark-to-market losses on TLT shorts.

ideas.key_risk: Pipeline trial failures or competition from next-generation FcRn antagonists could compress the premium multiple argenx commands.

ideas.theme: Bitcoin Mining / Energy Infrastructure / Analyst Upgrade
ideas.catalyst: Morgan Stanley raised its TeraWulf price target from $66.50 to $72 while maintaining an Overweight rating, citing improving hash rate economics and nuclear power cost advantages.
ideas.thesis: TeraWulf's differentiated access to low-cost nuclear power gives it a structural cost advantage over Bitcoin mining peers, providing resilience in volatile BTC environments. The Morgan Stanley PT raise to $72 signals growing institutional confidence in the clean-power mining model.
ideas.key_risk: A sharp Bitcoin price decline would compress mining economics and hurt WULF revenue significantly regardless of its cost structure advantages.

deals.headline: Madison Air to Acquire Airflow Technologies for $5.4 Billion
deals.description: HVAC and industrial airflow equipment manufacturer Madison Air announced a $5.4 billion all-cash acquisition of Airflow Technologies, expanding its commercial and industrial ventilation portfolio. The deal is expected to close in Q4 2026 pending regulatory review.
deals.impact: High - consolidates the industrial HVAC market; potential read-through for other HVAC and climate control companies.

deals.headline: Alibaba to Divest Videogame Business for $1.5B+
deals.description: Alibaba Group announced plans to sell its videogame business unit for at least $1.5 billion as part of a broader strategic restructuring to focus on core e-commerce and cloud businesses. The sale is expected to attract interest from Asian gaming conglomerates and private equity.
deals.impact: Medium - reduces Alibaba's conglomerate complexity discount; modestly positive for BABA valuation.

deals.headline: Kaos Capital Launches Activist Campaign at Capricor Therapeutics
deals.description: Activist investor Kaos Capital issued a letter demanding an immediate board meeting at Capricor Therapeutics following the FDA advisory panel's 9-3 vote against deramiocel for DMD cardiomyopathy. Kaos argues Capricor must preserve capital and pivot to acquisitions and licensing deals to broaden the pipeline.
deals.impact: High - creates near-term board and management uncertainty; likely to depress the stock further as capital preservation mode signals no near-term pipeline catalysts.
deals.source: BigGo Finance: Activist Kaos Capital at Capricor
